issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 2.1 asserts that phi(t) is strictly increasing on Lambda without imposing any restriction between h and delta^mu. By (2.7), on each interval I^j, phi(t) has derivative phi'(t) = ((h - delta^mu)/(h - delta)) P'((t - jh - delta)/(h - delta)). If h = delta^mu (which is explicitly allowed by the hypothesis h >= delta^mu in Theorem 2.1 and chosen in the numerical tests in Section 3.2), phi'(t) = 0 identically on every interval I^j of length h - delta, so phi is constant rather than strictly increasing on I^j, and psi_q'(x) vanishes identically across entire intervals rather than only at the endpoints. If h < delta^mu, phi is strictly decreasing on I^j.

issues.failure_explanation: In (3.7), the proof bounds |f(c_q^j)/N - (g_q circ Psi_q)(x)| by |s_{k+1} - s_k| <= (C_alpha / N)(N delta)^alpha, which presumes that (g_q circ Psi_q)(x) evaluates the 1D interpolant between the center c_q^j of the hypercube containing x and an adjacent center in the same row. However, as x varies over C_q^j, Psi_q(x) varies by order h, whereas the row-wise spacing is lambda_1 h <= O(h^2). Consequently, Psi_q(x) ranges across multiple rows, and the selection rule (2.29) picks an argmin index i whose corresponding center c_q^i is at Euclidean distance O(1) from c_q^j. The difference |f(c_q^j)/N - (g_q circ Psi_q)(x)| is therefore O(1/N) rather than O(h^alpha / N), yielding an unvanished overall error O(1). Additionally, the connected image Psi_q([0,1]^d) = [0, |lambda|_1] covers all gaps between row images, and switching rows via argmin produces O(1) jump discontinuities in f_N, violating the claimed C^2-continuity.
